posts.title: Sherman Oaks Fall 2026: New Openings Around the Street Fair
posts.description: A resident's guide to fall 2026 in Sherman Oaks: the Oct 18 Street Fair, new Ventura Blvd and Galleria openings, and how the corridor is stacking up.
posts.body:
The stretch of Ventura Boulevard between Kester Avenue and Van Nuys Boulevard has always been the busiest social spine in Sherman Oaks. What has changed in the past six months is what sits along it. A coworking floor at the Galleria, a golf simulator bar, a returning New York pizzeria a block off Woodman, a Mexican bakery in a former cafe space, and a new sushi marketplace on Sushi Row all landed on roughly the same walkable corridor. The 34th Annual Sherman Oaks Street Fair drops into the middle of it on Sunday, October 18.

For a resident who already knows the block, the interesting story this fall is not any single opening. It is that the Galleria has stopped behaving like a mall and started behaving like an anchor, and the food openings around it are clustering close enough that you can plan an entire Saturday without moving your car.

### The Galleria Is Doing More Than Selling Sneakers

The Sherman Oaks Galleria at 15301 Ventura Boulevard picked up two significant tenants this year, and neither is a retailer. Coworking operator Industrious signed a 22,000-square-foot deal across two floors, with 257 dedicated office seats and 50 on-demand seats, opening in April as its first Sherman Oaks location. The building is owned by Douglas Emmett, which also holds a Studio Plaza coworking floor in Burbank as the closest sibling location.

The second addition is Hapa Haus, a golf-simulator restaurant and bar planned for a November 2026 opening. Owner Alex Miyawaki filed plans for a 7,983-square-foot buildout with 69 indoor seats and 48 seats on a 1,526-square-foot covered patio, five simulators, and a Hawaiian-leaning menu. Miyawaki took up golf during the pandemic and told the local trade press he wanted to bring the simulator-bar format to the Valley.

Stacked together, that is roughly 30,000 square feet of new daytime and evening use inside a single building. The practical read for residents: the Galleria is turning into a place you actually pass through on a Tuesday, not just a weekend errand stop.

### Sushi Row Gets a Marketplace, Not Another Omakase Counter

Ventura Boulevard's Sushi Row is one of the more concentrated sushi corridors in the country, and the new arrival is not another chef's counter. Yama Sushi Marketplace signed for a 7,200-square-foot space at 15300 Ventura Boulevard #102G, directly across from the Galleria, for a late-summer 2026 opening. The concept is grab-and-go: sashimi-grade trays, bento boxes, an expanded sake selection, and plans for a full liquor license that would add Japanese whiskey, vodka, and gin to the beverage program.

CEO Scott Kohno, quoted in [What Now Los Angeles](https://whatnow.com/los-angeles/restaurants/yama-sushi-expanding-to-sherman-oaks-this-summer/), called Ventura Boulevard "ground zero for sushi in Los Angeles" and said the team had watched Valley customers drive to the West L.A. store for years. The kitchen is being sized for catering and delivery support to the brand's other locations, which means the Sherman Oaks store is also a production hub, not just a storefront. For neighbors, that translates into a real weeknight option: a quality sushi meal you take home in fifteen minutes instead of sitting through a two-hour prix fixe.

### The Street Fair Falls Right on Top of It

The 34th Sherman Oaks Street Fair runs Sunday, October 18, 2026, from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m., stretching along Ventura Boulevard between Kester Avenue and Van Nuys Boulevard. Admission is free. The fair is [organized by the Sherman Oaks Chamber of Commerce](https://shermanoaksstreetfair.org/) and is regularly described as the largest single-day festival in the San Fernando Valley, with reported attendance ranging from 50,000 to 100,000 in recent years.

Programming from the 33rd edition gives a reasonable preview of what to expect: a main stage with continuous live music, a Cham-BAR outdoor cocktail lounge formed by neighborhood spots including Buvette, Islands, The Local Peasant, and The Oaks Tavern, a carnival footprint with a Ferris wheel and obstacle course, and a pet zone hosting adoptions with LA Animal Services and rescues such as Callies Canine Rescue, Concerned Citizens Animal Rescue, Pawsitive Beginnings, and SoCal Golden Retriever Rescue.

The event, billed as the largest single-day festival in the San Fernando Valley, attracts between 50,000 and 100,000 attendees each year.

The geographic detail that matters this year is the overlap. The fair's western edge at Kester sits about a block from the Galleria's parking structure. Yama Sushi's storefront falls inside the closure. Burger She Wrote's Sherman Oaks location at 14245 Ventura is inside the closure. Gloria by La Era, opening at 13944 Ventura, is inside the closure. The Street Fair is not adjacent to the new openings. It runs directly through them.

### What's Opening Off the Boulevard, Too

Not every fall opening is on Ventura. Greco's New York Pizzeria is returning to Sherman Oaks at 4319 Woodman Avenue after the family-run brand's earlier Van Nuys Boulevard shop closed in 2016. The new location is a compact 1,000-square-foot storefront with counter service, an open kitchen, 28-inch pies, slices, and late-night hours. Co-owner Nico Grasu framed the move as a return rather than an expansion; the space had previously housed Santino's NY Pizza, which shut down at the end of March 2026.

A few notes on the food openings within a short walk of the fair route:

- Burger She Wrote, 14245 Ventura Blvd. Second location of the Fairfax-based smash burger shop founded in 2021 by professional skateboarder Don "Nuge" Nguyen and restaurateur Steven Arroyo, built around 100% American Wagyu and King's Hawaiian buns.

- Gloria by La Era, 13944 Ventura Blvd. New concept from Pastelerías La Era, a bakery with more than 20 locations in Mexico, taking the former Gracefully Fed space that closed in October 2025. Menu direction leaning on cakes, breads, and pastries.

- HoneyBaked Ham, Sherman Oaks. Opened by actor Leslie David Baker, who played Stanley on "The Office." Beyond the signature spiral-sliced ham and smoked turkey, the store carries sandwiches, salads, family meals, and catering.

- Popular, 18047 Ventura Blvd, a short drive west into Encino. The seventh concept from the Tel Aviv Restaurant Group opened earlier in 2026 in a 4,000-square-foot space with Mediterranean fusion and seafood-forward cooking under Executive Chef Dor Priezler. Worth knowing if the Street Fair crowds push you west.

### A Practical Order of Operations for October 18

If you live in Sherman Oaks and want to actually enjoy the density instead of just enduring the traffic, the fair rewards a specific sequence. This is how a resident might reasonably use the day:

- Park before 9:30 a.m. in the Galleria structure. It sits just outside the closure at Sepulveda and offers covered spots you can leave for the full day.

- Coffee and a pastry at Gloria by La Era, if the bakery is open by the fair date. It's a two-block walk east into the closure.

- Work the main stage and Cham-BAR between late morning and early afternoon while the crowd is still manageable.

- Break for a sit-down lunch at Burger She Wrote or a Yama Sushi grab-and-go tray on a Galleria bench. Both are inside the closed stretch.

- Late afternoon: cross back to the Galleria for a Hapa Haus preview if the November opening has softened to public tours, or pick up an early dinner takeout to bring home.

- If the fair energy is more than you want, drift west to Encino for dinner at Popular, or stay in for a Greco's late-night slice on Woodman.

That is not a schedule most residents would build from a generic fair guide. It works because the openings this year have concentrated within about six blocks.

### What This Actually Signals About the Neighborhood

The Ventura corridor between Kester and Sepulveda has spent most of the past decade defined by Sushi Row on the east and the Galleria on the west with a somewhat generic middle. The 2026 opening slate begins to fill that middle with format variety: a bakery, a smash burger, a grab-and-go sushi market, a coworking floor, a golf bar. None of those individually resets the neighborhood. Together they change how a resident moves through a normal weekend, and they change what a household considering a home nearby is actually buying access to.

For homeowners in the pocket streets south of Ventura and in the flats north of it, the practical effect is subtle. The block gets more useful on weekdays. Errands compress. The Galleria becomes a place you go for reasons that have nothing to do with retail. And the annual event that has defined the Sherman Oaks fall calendar for more than three decades now runs through a stretch of the boulevard that finally has enough new tenants to justify the crowd it draws.

### Let's Connect

If you already live in Sherman Oaks and are starting to think about what the changes on Ventura might mean for your home, or if you are watching the neighborhood from another part of the Valley and wondering how the corridor is evolving, Stacey Leahy is happy to talk it through. No pressure, no timeline, just a careful conversation about the block you actually live on.
